It breaks at x = 2, shooting off the grid, so (x − 2) is on the bottom; at x = 2 it goes down on the left and up on the right. Far out it falls back to the x-axis, y = 0, so the bottom has the higher degree. That is 2/(x − 2). The others: 2/(x + 2) would break at x = −2; −2/(x − 2) would go the other way at its asymptote; −2/(x + 2) would break at x = −2.
